overview: This table links each character's super attack to its finishing damage, multi-hit behavior, Domain Expansion, and ranking record.
description: Per-character finisher wiring: damage IDs for solo and tag-team super attacks, multi-hit behavior, linked domain expansion and the character-specific super-attack ranking record.

Id.simple: The name the game uses to find a character's super-attack settings. Some missions have that character use a different set.
Id.technical: FName member Id (exported as ID, ImportKeyField Id); runtime FindRow uses the DataTable row-map key rather than reading the member. AGameDataTableManager loads the one DataTable registered as CharacterSpecialAttackDataTable into CharacterSpecialAttackDataTables; every lookup walks that array and the first matching row wins. AGameCharacter::ResolveDataRows uses Overrides.SpecialAttackIdOverride when it is not None, otherwise CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterSpecialAttack; the override is copied from MissionCharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterSpecialAttack by GameMissionCharacter_CopyOverrideIds. A null result aborts ResolveDataRows. BattleCharacterAssetCollectors and GamePhase_BattleBase independently look up the same table with Character->Id_CharacterSpecialAttack, so they bypass the override and silently skip assets when the row is missing. ST_CP_051 and ST_CP_260 are reachable through mission overrides even though the base CharacterDataTable export does not reference them.

Id_GlossaryText_Name.simple: A place for the super attack's displayed name. Every available version leaves it empty, so its effect is unclear.
Id_GlossaryText_Name.technical: FName at GameDataTableRow_CharacterSpecialAttack.h:16. All 42 exported rows serialize None. No expression in the available Source/Plugins reads SpecialAttackRow.Id_GlossaryText_Name. Every Id_GlossaryText_Name consumer found is instead on FGameDataTableRow_Character (for example Setup.CharacterRow->Id_GlossaryText_Name feeding GetGameTextById), a distinct field at row +0x10. Retail Blueprint graphs are unavailable, so this is a source-level negative result rather than proof that retail has no use.

Id_Damage_SpecialTagCombo.simple: Which damage the tag-team special combo uses for its finisher. The game checks whether it will defeat the target, then deals that damage.
Id_Damage_SpecialTagCombo.technical: FName key into DamageDataTables (DamageDataTable1..5; first matching row wins). State 6 takes it from Performers[0] at sequence exit: IsLethalSequenceDamage(..., bIgnoreStock=false) requires the projected hit to reduce the target to <=0 HP and the target to be out of stock (no ActionControllerSlot181 preservation and GetStockAfterLoss <= 0). The same ID is then passed to ApplySequenceDamage on State()->Target. ApplySequenceDamage looks up the Damage row across all five shards, queues AddMultiHit at zero delay with Flags78=0x23, and still queues the request with a null DamageRow if the ID does not resolve; a null row makes the lethal prediction false. 30/42 exported rows set this ID (the 12 CN rows are None, ST_CP_051 uses its own ST_ ID), and all non-None IDs resolve in the available Damage shards.

Id_Damage_SoloSpecialAttack.simple: The damage used to finish a solo super attack. The game checks whether it will defeat an opponent's team, then deals it to the caught opponent or opponents.
Id_Damage_SoloSpecialAttack.technical: FName key into the same five DamageDataTables shards. State 5 reads the finisher's cached row for IsAnyTeamDefeated with bIgnoreStock=true (HP check only; stock is checked separately through team cost and GetRemainingCharacterStock), then at sequence end calls ApplySequenceDamage once per KnockOut.KnockedOut loser. That victim list is produced by the multi-hit collector, so this field's effect is coupled to bMultiHitSoloSpecialAttack. Missing damage rows make IsLethalSequenceDamage return false and ApplySequenceDamage queue a request with DamageRow=null. 30/42 exported rows set this ID; the 12 CN rows are None, CP_050/CP_130/CP_160 reuse CP_010's damage, and ST_CP_051 has its own ST_ ID; all non-None IDs resolve in the available shards.

bMultiHitSoloSpecialAttack.simple: Turn this on to make a solo super hit every remaining opponent it catches. Turn it off to hit one chosen opponent, the other selected target or the main target.
bMultiHitSoloSpecialAttack.technical: Bool, constructor default false. AGameCharacter::IsMultiHitSoloSpecialAttackEnabled returns SpecialAttackRow->bMultiHitSoloSpecialAttack without a null check (the base IGameActorInterface implementation returns false); ResolveDataRows guarantees the cache on resolved AGameCharacter instances. FStudioBattleSystem310::UpdateSoloSpecialAttackFinish first removes defeated victims. When true it copies the whole remaining victim list into KnockOut.KnockedOut and stops processing further attackers. When false it selects one victim: a valid, visible secondary target if present, else a valid primary target, falling back to index 0; the selection branch is only used when more than one victim remains. Export has CP_020 as the sole true row; the other 41 rows, including all 12 CN rows and both ST_ rows, are false.

Id_DomainExpansion.simple: The Domain Expansion tied to this super attack, when the character has one. It sets the domain stage and finisher placement, with one character using tag-team placement and changing stage later.
Id_DomainExpansion.technical: FName key into DomainExpansionDataTables. ResolveDataRows does an optional lookup and caches the result in DomainExpansionRow; None leaves that cache null and skips asset preload. BattleCharacterAssetCollectors and GamePhase_BattleBase resolve SpecialAttack -> DomainExpansion -> Map and add DomainMap->MiniMapFileName only when Id_Map is non-None; available rows CP_020/CP_030/CP_050 have no map, while CP_130/CP_140/CP_260/ST_CP_260 do. State 7 makes a fresh lookup of this ID for the sequence transform: a resolved row with a non-None Id_Map selects GetDomainExpansionTransform unless IsNotCP130() is false; CP_130 and the absent-row/absent-map cases use GetTagComboTransform(0). IsNotCP130 compares the caster's model name to CP_130. Other state-7 logic uses the cached DomainExpansionRow (HasDomainMap checks its Id_Map): non-CP130 requests the domain stage in substate 2, while CP130 requests it at exit. A character that actually enters state 7 therefore needs a resolvable Id_DomainExpansion even though ResolveDataRows itself permits None. 7/42 rows set this ID and all resolve in the available DomainExpansion export.

RankingRecord.simple: Which numbered super-attack ranking record this character can earn. It is earned by landing a Super Cursed Energy hit and appears on the results.
RankingRecord.technical: EGameRankingRecord (uint8) stored per character; constructor default None. EvaluateRankingRecords iterates every RankingRecordDataTable row and, for the numbered SuperCursedEnergyAttack_01..27 cases, awards a record only when this field equals that row's RankingRecord and the player's SuperCursedEnergyAttack_Hit log (Myself, Send, counted as int32) is at least that row's PrizeThreshold; the enum byte is appended to OutRecords. In the available RankingRecord export all 27 numbered rows exist with PrizeThreshold 1. None or an unnumbered enum value cannot satisfy this branch; the generic SuperCursedEnergyAttack record is a separate case and is not driven by this field. 28/42 exported rows set a numbered value (CP_051 and ST_CP_051 both map to _17; CP_270 maps to _27) and 14 rows are None.

notes: The base export has 42 rows: 40 character IDs plus ST_CP_051 and ST_CP_260 mission variants. The 42 per-character JSON files are one-row subsets of the same export, not additional shards. Available Content is partial, so this is not a claim about every retail character or Blueprint reference.
Id_GlossaryText_Name on this row is distinct from CharacterDataTable.Id_GlossaryText_Name; no source consumer of the special-attack copy was identifiable. All exported values are None.

All non-None Id_Damage_* and Id_DomainExpansion references resolve in the available DamageDataTable1..5, DomainExpansionDataTable and MapDataTable exports. None is the no-damage/no-domain sentinel on all 12 CN rows, and CP_020/CP_030/CP_050 have DomainExpansion rows without an Id_Map.

Lookup precedence differs by consumer: AGameCharacter applies SpecialAttackIdOverride (from the mission row), while BattleCharacterAssetCollectors and GamePhase_BattleBase use the base Character->Id_CharacterSpecialAttack. Character lookups walk the manager's table array with first-match precedence and cache SpecialAttackRow for state 5/6/7, damage and ranking.

Evidence is reconstructed C++ plus the read-only DataTable exports. Source comments with retail RVAs are provenance hints, not byte-match verdicts; no retail Blueprint graph, cooked binary or live-game check was performed.

usages.detail: Registers the CharacterSpecialAttackDataTable asset under the FName used to build CharacterSpecialAttackDataTables.
ResolveDataRows looks up the row with SpecialAttackIdOverride if set, else CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterSpecialAttack, and caches it in SpecialAttackRow; a miss aborts setup.
Copies MissionCharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterSpecialAttack into the override, allowing ST_CP_051/ST_CP_260 rows to replace the character default.
Resolves Id_DomainExpansion optionally and caches the DomainExpansion row; None leaves the cache null.
Looks up the special-attack row from the base character ID for asset collection, bypassing the setup override.
Joins SpecialAttack -> DomainExpansion -> Map to collect the domain map's MiniMapFileName.
Battle-phase preloading independently follows SpecialAttack.Id_DomainExpansion to the domain map's minimap texture.
Uses the finisher's Id_Damage_SoloSpecialAttack for team-defeat lethality prediction with bIgnoreStock=true.
Applies Id_Damage_SoloSpecialAttack once per knocked-out loser at the end of the solo super sequence.
Uses bMultiHitSoloSpecialAttack to choose all remaining victims or one selected victim for KnockOut.KnockedOut.
Uses Performers[0].Id_Damage_SpecialTagCombo for lethal prediction with bIgnoreStock=false.
Applies Performers[0].Id_Damage_SpecialTagCombo to the tag-combo target.
Shared ApplySequenceDamage helper resolves either damage ID across all Damage shards and queues AddMultiHit with flags 0x23.
Freshly resolves Id_DomainExpansion to choose the domain or tag-combo sequence transform, with the CP_130 exception.
CP130 domain state requests its stage from the cached DomainExpansionRow->Id_Map at exit.
Matches the player's RankingRecord to numbered RankingRecordDataTable rows after the Super hit threshold is reached.
Appends the matched RankingRecord enum byte to the earned-result records.
